notFound: no meta-analysis or systematic review of valuing or pursuing happiness and well-being (both agents, three bases)

no direct, preregistered or multi-lab replication of Mauss et al. 2011 Study 2: only an undergraduate thesis of 19 people, another task, null (Coles 2015, no DOI); Hansenne 2021 and Mahmoodi Kahriz 2019 replicate correlations only
no replication of Wegner et al. 1993 on mood

no Egyptian, Arab or Middle Eastern / North African sample on valuing or pursuing happiness: a few Middle Eastern and Mauritanian students pooled, never analysed apart, in Mahmoodi Kahriz 2019; only happiness-program trials in Arab countries
the text of Mauss 2011's correction (APA 403) and the journal version of Huang 2024 (figures checked only against the preprint)
not kept, no abstract anywhere: Gentzler 2019, Wong 2019, Liang 2026 (interdependence as moderator), the Nature Reviews Psychology 2025 review; Ludwigs 2017 (abstract ambiguous)
not kept: Schooler et al. 2003 (chapter, no result in its abstract); Kim 2025 (rests on ego depletion, a contested effect)

found.note: contradicts c2: trying to make one's mood better works with a free mind; only under mental load does mood move the opposite way. A condition, not a law; no replication on mood found
contradicts c2: students who wanted to become happier, and kept the effort, gained more from happiness activities (will not randomized; small effects; the authors design these activities)
contradicts c1, c2 and c3: in 100 French women, wanting more happiness for tomorrow went with more intense happiness the next day, through savoring (diary, association; abstract read on HAL)
supports c2 in the book's sense (« a negative experience »): induced valuing of happiness raised loneliness; same lab as Mauss 2011, no replication
supports c2: stressing the importance of happiness raised rumination after a failure; independent lab, no replication
against a cultural switch: in Japan valuing happiness goes with more rumination, once more strongly among the most interdependent. Ford 2015 cannot become « in Asia it is the reverse »

offered against « c3 contradicted »; not taken: its « experiential attachment » items are worry items (« I worried about my positive emotions fading », full text). Kept as a nuance: doing one's best to stay happy helped one group, harmed the other only through worry

the card: r = .24 was a random-intercept correlation from the preprint (dropped); the plain wish is followed by a little more negative affect as well as positive (exploratory); one item near its ceiling (mean 6.1 of 7)
fragile main support of c2: about 17 women per cell, effects at p = .02 to .05; its correction unread (APA 403), three concordant clues point to the title; Study 2 figures from the author manuscript
Mauss & Ford 2026, narrative review by the same lab: the consequences depend on how people pursue happiness (five aspects, not only worry): backs the nuance « it is how you chase it »
Catalino, Tov & Hoorn 2026: five preregistered studies, prioritizing positivity goes with more well-being and more hypomania; not added (Hansenne 2021 already carries it)
Conner & Reid 2011: rating one's happiness often does not lower it on average, but does among the more depressed: no takeaway that says « watch your happiness »
White, Uttl & Holder 2019: programs to become happier help a little once small-sample bias is corrected (r ≈ .10): indirect against c2
Lambert et al. 2021: the only Arab trial found (120 Emirati students): a 6-week happiness program raised positive emotion, nothing else, no backfire; indirect
Basurrah et al. 2022: positive psychology programs in 10 Arab countries appear effective, with risk of bias (systematic review): applicability, indirect
Lou et al. 2025, 43 countries: more religious cultures idealize happiness less; the premise « always wanting more » may fit an Egyptian audience less
Valdivia-Salas et al. 2022, 168 Spanish women, cross-sectional: valuing happiness goes with more negative affect; weak support for c1, not added

counterEvidence.conclusion: ⚖️ low holds; nothing reaches moderate. Taken: c2 rebalanced (Wegner, Lyubomirsky, Pavani against; Mauss 2012, McGuirk for), still mixed; culture is no switch (Takai); card line corrected. Not taken: c3 « mixed »: Sahdra's attachment items are worry items, Huang's cost is tiny and exploratory. c3 stays contradicted, low; the nuance becomes « it is how you chase it ».
